paras.t: Migraines have a lot of triggers. If your neck is one of yours, that's the part Casey Morgan D.C. can work on.

bullets.text: In and out in minutes, not rushed

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: If your migraines come with a tight neck

paras.t: Maybe your migraines tend to follow a stiff neck or a long week at the computer. Maybe the pain starts at the base of your skull before it settles behind one eye. Maybe you've noticed they hit harder when your shoulders are up around your ears.
If any of that sounds familiar, it's worth finding out whether your neck is part of the picture.

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: The neck is one trigger, not the only one

paras.t: Migraines can be set off by sleep, stress, hormones, food, light, and a long list of other things. A doctor or neurologist is the right person to help you sort those out.

What a chiropractor can look at is the neck. When the joints and muscles at the top of the neck are tight or not moving well, they can feed into headaches, and for some people they're part of what sets off a migraine.

callouts.title: Dr. Morgan won't promise to fix your migraines.
callouts.text: He'll examine your neck, tell you whether it looks like part of the problem, and treat that part if it is.

sections.name: Header – Find it, fix it, keep it from coming bac
sections.title: Find it, fix it, keep it from coming back

paras.t: Keep your doctor in the loop. Chiropractic care here works alongside whatever your doctor or neurologist is doing for your migraines, not instead of it.

bullets.body: A full history of your migraines (how often, what sets them off, what you've tried) and an exam of your neck and upper back. Digital X-rays if your exam calls for them.
Adjustments to the neck and upper back when the exam shows they're involved. Dr. Morgan starts gentle.
Once the neck is moving well, most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks.

sections.name: First Visit Section
sections.title: Your first visit, start to finish

paras.t: First visit runs about 30 minutes. After that, most visits take a few minutes. Dr. Morgan built the practice around working people.

steps.title: We find out what is actually happening
steps.text: Full history and exam. What hurts, what you have already tried, what you want to get back to doing. Any necessary digital X-rays, taken on site.

steps.title: Dr. Morgan shows you the imaging, same day
steps.text: He marks it up and walks you through it right there. You will see what he sees. Most patients get their first adjustment the same visit.

steps.title: You come back for the full report
steps.text: Within a few days, Dr. Morgan lays out what he found and exactly what he recommends. What it will take, how long, and what it costs. Then you decide.

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: How long until this actually feels better

paras.t: Most people want a number before they start. Dr. Morgan will give you one, just not before he has examined you and looked at your imaging. He will not guess.
What he can tell you up front is how it usually goes, including the part most offices skip: the first two weeks are uneven.
If you are only trying to get out of pain, a shorter plan can do that. If you want it to stay fixed, it takes about 90 days. Dr. Morgan will give you both options and let you pick.

tags.text: Inconsistent, and that's normal. You'll have a good day and think it's fixed, then a bad one and think it's not working. Dr. Morgan warns you about this on day one. Real change usually starts around the end of week two, and better sleep is often the first thing people notice.

The bulk of the plan. A typical plan is about 24 visits over 90 days, two to three times a week at the start, then less often as you improve. Some people need fewer. Dr. Morgan checks your progress along the way.
Most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks. Some stop entirely. Dr. Morgan will tell you when you're there.

faqs.a: It depends on whether your neck is part of what's setting them off. Dr. Morgan examines your neck and tells you. If it is, he treats that part. He won't promise to stop your migraines.

faqs.q: Should I stop seeing my doctor?
faqs.a: No. Chiropractic care works alongside your doctor or neurologist, not instead of them.

faqs.q: Do you adjust during a migraine?
faqs.a: Tell the front desk when you book or when you arrive. Dr. Morgan will decide what makes sense that day, and gentle is always the starting point.
Only if your exam calls for it. If Dr. Morgan takes them, they happen on site at your first visit.

faqs.q: When should I go to the ER instead?
faqs.a: If a headache is the worst of your life, comes on suddenly, or comes with weakness, confusion, trouble speaking, vision loss, or a stiff neck with fever, go to an emergency room. Those aren't a typical migraine.
